_about: PARKED. What each fighter of the launch pair ships with in the next update, and what waits (../launch-pair-movesets.md). Fighter keys are the neutral working ids (protagonist, rival) until Orb names the pair. Counts are authored sketches. Game Design's launch-pair-plan.md sets the scope. Checked against HEAD a56187a.

posed._about: poses in Animation's packs at HEAD a56187a (data/anim/waves and data/anim/poses.json), all parked or behind flags

ships.pack: wave1 (the body ram re-posed in rival2)

ships.piece: the barrage: six hands, the charged brace, the kiting turn (wave 6)
ships.pack: rival1 (six hands, the channel, the kiting turn)

ships.piece: Blow for Blow (ships with the alchemy framework)
ships.pack: rival1 (the brace); rival2 (the body hook, the rib shot)

wave 3: the ping-pong and curved entries (curved flight)
wave 4: grabs and throws (the held state)
the rest of the kit, finishers, form cinematics, tail pieces

energyKinds.why: a spread on a marked patch tells the rival where he may not stand: his hierarchy made playable
his barrage in one press: five shards from one charged shot punish a late dodge

glasses.dependsOn: nothing: no move, gate, reach or outcome reads them, and no piece touches them
glasses.glare: render only, on cues that exist: the taunt, On the Chin's plant, a signature's wind-up, a Pride threshold, the seal break (a cracked lens). No beat is added for it
keptClear: no piece pushes the glasses at the bridge or puts two fingers to the temple
no stance folds or steeples the hands before the face
the headbutt leads with the brow: glasses knocked askew or off by a hit are Legal's GO and Art's to draw

ownEntries.look: a tumble that opens into the blow, limbs extended, at most one revolution, never a tight spinning ball (Legal)
a cartwheel step on the ground into the blow

ships.piece: two hands of his own and his charged brace

later: heat beats and the Open Hand cinematic

energyKinds.why: a martial artist's precision: the stick bends it round cover or a guard, drawing his arcs
a bank shot: the craftsman's version of the same idea

openForOrb: teleports: he is the natural owner; nothing here uses one; a teleported flurry can be a finisher variant later

onTheChin.rules: docs/design/spec-wounds.md section 3: hold context 12 ticks at Pride 60+; up to 4 s; 3 hits or 1 signature; nothing moves him; 20 ticks to let go; 25 s cooldown; a throw beats it

beats.look: arms open a little forward and slightly below shoulder height, not a flat cross; chin level; eyes open

beats.pause: the bank, else live with a cut

limits: arms a little forward of the body line and slightly below shoulder height: never a flat cross, never behind the body
no head thrown back, no closed eyes
the rear thigh at most 45 degrees back
the arms-open stance is his alone

finishers._about: Two rows in the live finishers' form (data/combat/finishers.json, combat.finishers/1), ready to sit in its 'finishers' list, with the select block that goes with them. Checked on a scratch copy of HEAD a56187a against tools/schemas/combat-finishers.schema.json. Durations are seconds in multiples of 3 ticks, as the live rows; the contest resolves 66 ticks after it opens

select._note: the keys are roster ids (upper case by the schema's pattern): stand-ins for the folder names Simulation picks at the split

rows.character: The rival (feeds on collateral; Pride). He takes his distance, puts three volleys into the loser until he gives way, walks in unhurried and ends it by hand. No beam.

bends.pride: the volley count rises with Pride
bends.apex: the walk becomes a long stillness and one blow
bends.held: after the blow he lowers the arm and turns half away: the winner's stand takes over (fin.held)

rows._runsToday: every beat is a live op, so the row validates and plays as it stands. The three barrage beats are render cues with no damage until Encounter has a finisher volley (the volley arg is its input: 25 a volley, 75 before the contest); a strike beat cannot stand in, because a damaging strike places the striker at contact

rows.character: The Protagonist (pressured by collateral). He catches the loser, flies round him four times with a different blow from a new side each time, rises, and ends it with a one-hand blast at point-blank range, sent skyward and away from the people below.

bends.heat: three flights when Heated, four when Simmering, five when Boiling (a proposal for Game Design)
bends.curvedFlight: each flight is wave 3's spiral round the loser once curved flight exists; a straight crossing until then

rows._runsToday: every beat is a live op, so the row validates and plays as it stands: four straight crossings (side cross) with a blow at the end of each. The damage before the contest is 100 and the last blow 60, as the live kai finisher (30, 30, 40 and 60)
rows._legal: drawn the whole way, no vanish, no afterimage that hides him; one-hand blast, never a two-hand push from the chest, a sphere in a palm or hands at a hip; a local column, no pillar, no darkening sky, no mushroom cloud, no planet-scale sphere, no shouted name with it; Orb's scale 7 of 10; no roar

newArgs._about: read by nobody today and ignored by the live ops; each is a hint for a later slice
newArgs.cue.volley: the rival's barrage beats: {dmg, shape, count} for Encounter's finisher volley
newArgs.finRush.gait: walk: Animation's walk-in instead of a dash
newArgs.strike.slot: flurry: the strike piece is drawn from _flurryPool, a different one and a new side each time
newArgs.finalBlow.slot, limb, shape: the last blow's piece: an ender by hand, or a charged blast from one hand
